title: VPC-aware cost suggester with sandboxed apply and staged enforcement
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a VPC/private-friendly recommendations engine that proposes batching and KV-prefix caching changes, lets operators validate effects in a sandboxed dry-run, and then applies changes via a staged enforcement flow with automatic revert on safety signals. This must respect private deployment constraints (no telemetry offloading, customer KMS policies, and offline-only admin paths).

Scope: recommendation generation, sandboxed/dry-run apply, policy check layer, staged enforcement (canary -> full), revert triggers and audit logging integration. Exclude UI polish; focus on infra, config semantics, and API contract for Private/VPC installs.
acceptance_criteria: Engine can emit batching/caching recommendations for VPC tenants with rationale and estimated token-cost delta.
Operators can execute a dry-run that simulates request-level batching and prefix-cache hits without sending telemetry outside the customer's network.
A staged apply path exists: staging canary -> monitored ramp -> full apply; each step requires policy checks and explicit operator confirmation in private installs.
Automatic rollback triggers on QoS regressions (latency increase beyond threshold, error rate spike) or policy violations with an audit trail written to customer-provided storage/KMS references.
All changes are recorded in the deployment audit log and surface in Console (for hosted) or local audit endpoint (for Private) with links to the recommendation and simulation report.
Config artifacts are signed and support an offline apply flow for air-gapped customers (tarball + signature) and a documented manual verification checklist.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Recommendation API - implement VPC-aware heuristic generator that uses historical sequence length distribution and per-route SLOs to produce candidate batching and KV caching configs.
Phase 2: Sandbox simulation - add a local simulator that can run replayed traces inside the customer's network boundary; output estimated latency/cost and prefix-cache hit-rate maps.

Phase 3: Policy guard - build a policy layer that validates candidate configs against tenant policy (no external telemetry, allowed quantization levels, KMS constraints) and returns a compliance report.
Phase 4: Staged apply + revert - implement canary orchestration hooks, metric watchers, and safe revert logic with signed change artifacts and audit events.
Phase 5: Private deployment packaging - provide an offline artifact (signed tarball) and a CLI apply that verifies signature and policies before mutating runtime config.
Phase 6: Observability - wire simulation and live apply metrics to Console dashboards and to local audit sinks for Private installs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for recommendation heuristics with synthetic traffic shapes.
Integration test: replay recorded VPC tenant traces in simulator and compare simulated vs actual metrics in a staging cluster.
Canary test: deploy to 1% of routes behind feature flag for 48h with automated checks (p99 latency, error rate, token per request).
Security test: verify offline apply flow rejects tampered artifacts and that no telemetry egress occurs during simulation (network policy enforcement).
Chaos test: induce KV cache eviction and GPU preemption to validate revert triggers.
rollout_plan: Internal alpha: infra team only in private dev VPC (2 weeks).
Private beta: 3 select customers with signed NDAs, offline apply flow tested (4 weeks).
Hosted preview: limited opt-in in hosted for non-sensitive tenants with telemetry allowed and Console visibility (2 weeks).
General availability: gated by security review sign-off and post-beta incident review.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Simulator mismatch could produce misleading cost estimates. Mitigation: require replay-based validation and conservative default reductions; surface uncertainty bands in reports.
Risk: Offline apply CLI may be misused and cause downtime. Mitigation: require signed artifacts, operator confirmation, and pre-apply dry-checks; include an emergency rollback artifact in the bundle.

Risk: Policy enforcement complexity across customer KMS/HSM variants. Mitigation: adopt pluggable policy adapters and include common templates for major KMS vendors; require security review for new adapter.
Risk: Private installs cannot rely on hosted metrics for rollback decisions. Mitigation: implement local metric collectors and lightweight watchers that can run on prometheus pushgateway or local DB.
